newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares fall in mid-trade on foreign selloff.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares fall in mid-trade on foreign selloff.

text.p: Persistent foreign selling and poor first quarter profits of companies sent Manila's main stock market index reeling on Wednesday by mid-session by 30.21 points, or 1.12 percent, to 2,678.23 points.

"People who were not able to get out of the market yesterday are doing so today. Sentiment is very weak due to companies' profits that were below expectations," said Lawrence de Leon, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils.
Traders said foreign selling was evident as B shares of San Miguel Corp and Manila Electric Co (Meralco) posted losses. B shares are reserved for foreign investors.
Both San Miguel and Meralco reported lower-than-expected first quarter earnings after the market closed on Tuesday when the main index fell to a two-year low, closing 128.87 points down at 2,708.44.
Traders said the market was focused on domestic corporate developments with foreign investors seeing the Dow's rise as a cue to shift to the more attractive U.S. market.
The Dow closed sharply higher by 179 points on Tuesday as worries over rising interest rates ebbed.
